name: Cert Lifecycle
description: ITIL-correct certificate renewal: Splunk detects near-expiry certs, a standard change is raised per cert type (pre-approved for non-invasive reloads, approval required for restarts), AAP renews and validates TLS. An incident is only created if renewal fails.

host.description: Hostname of the service with the expiring cert

extra_vars.short_description: Certificate renewal: ${trigger.service} on ${trigger.host} (PEM - reload, zero downtime)
extra_vars.implementation_plan:
1. Request new PEM certificate from Vault CA.
2. Replace cert and key files on ${trigger.host}.
3. Reload nginx (zero downtime — no service restart).
4. Automated TLS validation.
extra_vars.test_plan: OpenSSL TLS handshake check on ${trigger.host}:${trigger.port} verifying subject, issuer, and expiry > 7 days.

extra_vars.short_description: Certificate renewal: ${trigger.service} on ${trigger.host} (Java keystore - RESTART REQUIRED)
extra_vars.implementation_plan:
1. Request new certificate from Vault CA.
2. Convert PEM to PKCS12 and import into Java keystore.
3. RESTART Tomcat service (brief downtime expected).
4. Automated TLS validation.
extra_vars.test_plan: OpenSSL TLS handshake check on ${trigger.host}:${trigger.port} verifying subject, issuer, and expiry > 7 days.

extra_vars.work_notes: Change request rejected. Certificate on ${trigger.host}:${trigger.port} still has ${trigger.days_remaining} days remaining. Manual renewal required before expiry.
